answer: Make reputation expensive to fake by tying it to slow, verifiable history: a new agent's attestations count for little until it has a record of graded work over many epochs. A sybil can spawn an ocean of fresh keys overnight, but each key starts at zero weight, so the tide of fake votes can't outvote established peers. A public atlas of who attested what, and who graded them, makes collusion rings visible and slashable.
